jobs.page: 01_Survival/Moon 3 Day 17 - Let the Sole Hold the Wrap.md
jobs.scene: Checking the new heel keeper on the retained bast sole, with both low skin covers fitted.
jobs.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Landscape daily illustration for Humanity Handbook. Fine brown ink and richly natural watercolour on warm ivory paper, matching original Day 1 visual language. Late autumn in low-elevation northern Iberian wooded limestone valley.
Image 1 gives ONLY original man's IDENTITY AND PAINT STYLE. NEVER copy its old lean-to, nakedness, tools or camp geometry. Image 2 gives ONLY DATED CLOTHING. Same lean ordinary adult around thirty, dark wavy ear-length hair, short beard, smooth human skin no tattoos/scars, natural hands and exactly two arms/two legs.
CLOTHING MUST PERSIST: ONE worn dull TAN skin body wrap, brown hair inward, both shoulders, sleeveless, overlapping front, irregular hem above knees. Small repair at anatomical LEFT shoulder, upper chest tie below throat, light waist line/hip keeper. Same plain grey-brown rabbit crown with tan-brown hair-in side/ear/nape extension. HUMAN face/forehead open; no animal ears, muzzle, rabbit face, hood or fox shoulder strip. Old fox panel is ALL in cap. Both grass torso screens stored and absent. Underlying waist layers concealed.
BOTH feet fully ENCLOSED in LOW pale-tan skin coverings, inward hair and modest grass lining, toes and heels CLOSED, tops just above ankles; original woven BAST SOLES remain BELOW/OUTSIDE, with visible woven margins and low ties. No exposed toes, tall boots, leather outsole or leggings. Lower legs and much arms bare. No new cloak, sleeves, armour, metal, bow, finished pot, extra skins or huge food store.
No labels, text, border or watermark. Chosen one actual moment, no multi-day collage. Cropped natural backgrounds do not survey new camp positions. If not expressly requested, NO home/shelter, lean-to, piled roof branches, cave furnishings, hearth or indoor fire.
Chosen moment AFTER layers are reunited, before the short outing. Man seated naturally on a low dry natural stone, one foot gently raised onto a lower stone and other foot planted, BOTH enclosed shoes clearly visible. Hands adjust a short plain plant-cord keeper at SIDE/REAR of bast sole on raised foot, not stitching a new skin or tying tightly round ankle. Old bast wearing layer remains outside pale-tan cover. Natural simple two-legged anatomy with clearly readable knees; no third limb. Background just softly washed limestone face and a few tree trunks on dry ground; no home, old lean-to or screen, no river water at feet. Cap/body wrap/low covers precisely Image 2. No weapon or pot. Focus load carried by existing sole and usable layers, not a new boot pattern.

jobs.scene: A controlled approach with the newly made compact four-pronged wooden fishing spear from dry bank footing.
jobs.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Landscape daily illustration for Humanity Handbook. Fine brown ink and richly natural watercolour on warm ivory paper, matching original Day 1 visual language. Late autumn in low-elevation northern Iberian wooded limestone valley.
Image 1 gives ONLY original man's IDENTITY AND PAINT STYLE. NEVER copy its old lean-to, nakedness, tools or camp geometry. Image 2 gives ONLY DATED CLOTHING. Same lean ordinary adult around thirty, dark wavy ear-length hair, short beard, smooth human skin no tattoos/scars, natural hands and exactly two arms/two legs.
CLOTHING MUST PERSIST: ONE worn dull TAN skin body wrap, brown hair inward, both shoulders, sleeveless, overlapping front, irregular hem above knees. Small repair at anatomical LEFT shoulder, upper chest tie below throat, light waist line/hip keeper. Same plain grey-brown rabbit crown with tan-brown hair-in side/ear/nape extension. HUMAN face/forehead open; no animal ears, muzzle, rabbit face, hood or fox shoulder strip. Old fox panel is ALL in cap. Both grass torso screens stored and absent. Underlying waist layers concealed.
BOTH feet fully ENCLOSED in LOW pale-tan skin coverings, inward hair and modest grass lining, toes and heels CLOSED, tops just above ankles; original woven BAST SOLES remain BELOW/OUTSIDE, with visible woven margins and low ties. No exposed toes, tall boots, leather outsole or leggings. Lower legs and much arms bare. No new cloak, sleeves, armour, metal, bow, finished pot, extra skins or huge food store.
No labels, text, border or watermark. Chosen one actual moment, no multi-day collage. Cropped natural backgrounds do not survey new camp positions. If not expressly requested, NO home/shelter, lean-to, piled roof branches, cave furnishings, hearth or indoor fire.
Image 3 supplies MULTI-PRONGED FISHING SPEAR appearance ONLY. Day 79 chosen BEFORE the catch: full man with BOTH feet in low enclosed pelt covers on original bast soles, planted on a broad DRY level bank well back from edge. Clear shallow near-side slow-water pocket with visible pale bottom and just ONE small generic fish below surface. He holds ONE ordinary-length WOOD shaft with compact head split into exactly FOUR modestly spreading WOOD PRONGS, small simple lower binding. Four points share same shaft, no separate metal tines or stone/barbed inserts. Points lowered near water surface, not an impaled fish, no violent kill or pile of catches. No atlatl, stone spear, ordinary single-point spear or second tool in frame.
Natural balanced controlled stance, no deep wading, lunging off bank or wet feet. Human face open under correct cap, tan hair-inward body wrap loose at shoulders, all toes enclosed. Background woodland and limestone is atmospheric, not a new watercourse map. No camp building. Make the four visible wooden points readable and small enough to remain useful rather than huge fantasy fork.
input_roles: planned plate supplies four-prong wooden head appearance, now made in story

attempts.review: Four modest wooden prongs visible on a separate long fishing spear. Both covered feet remain on dry bank; fish alive in water before catch, no impalement. Existing wrap and cap, natural hands and two legs. No other spear repurposed or finished pottery.

jobs.scene: A conceptual separation of clean food, dirty skin work and manageable carrying loads.
jobs.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Humanity Handbook principle plate, navy ink and restrained pastel watercolour on warm ivory paper. Image 1 provides graphic style ONLY, not its digging-stick object. Title exactly "LARGE-GAME PROCESSING".
Three simple separated conceptual work studies across wide page with whitespace, not a valley map or actual inventory. LEFT clean bark sheets with a few small CLOSED folded bark food parcels, lightly indicated open-air space around them, label "CLEAN FOOD". MIDDLE one modest grey-brown FUR-ON SKIN MARGIN lying on a separate low simple twig support, no blood or tissue, label "SEPARATE SKIN WORK". RIGHT one pair of generic clothed HANDS holding a modest closed bark parcel at comfortable height, label "MANAGEABLE LOADS"; no full human body or extra anatomy. Small bottom line exactly "PROMPT HANDLING • COOLING • TRANSPORT".
No animal carcass, slaughter, cutaway anatomy, red meat, entrails, knives in use, weights, preservation promise, refrigerator, vehicle, pots, cloth sacks, metal, buildings or large hide clothing. This diagram explains separation and work after a result, not a hunting technique or safe shelf-life recipe. No arrows merging dirty skin and clean food. It grants no full hide or food stock to story protagonist. Readable simple labels and restrained material amounts.

attempts.review: Three separate conceptual studies of bark food parcels, separate skin work and manageable loads. No flesh, carcass or kill. Generic cropped carrier is not the protagonist; skin study is a principle diagram, not his actual hide allocation, dimensions or inventory.
